grange_cook.text: Grangetown's finest. Fish, chips and a good gossip, all included in the price.
Cardiff grew rich on coal. By 1913 it was one of the busiest coal ports in the world, and the dockers needed feeding.
In Cardiff, if something is good you say it is tidy. Do not ask me why. A really good portion of chips is tidy.

then.text: Open the post, bach. Even the brown ones. Especially the brown ones.

else.text: There was a drawer. For a year, every brown envelope went into the drawer. I told myself I'd look at them when I had the money to fix it.
Then a man came to the door. That was the day I learnt a drawer is not a plan.
What would you tell Gwyn a year ago?
options: Open the post and ask for help early
Keep the drawer shut, it'll sort itself
Borrow from someone to cover it

then.text: Yes. Debts grow when ignored, and the people who can help are glad to hear early, not late.
I wish someone had told me. It never sorts itself, it gets interest.
Borrowing to cover borrowing is how a small hole becomes a big one. Slow down and talk to someone first.

else.text: There's free, confidential debt advice from Citizens Advice, StepChange and MoneyHelper. Nobody there is going to tut. They've seen drawers far worse than mine.
Asking for help isn't weakness. It's the quickest way out. I should know. I paid for all those lost months.
Take these. Welsh cakes, still warm.
Noted in the Almanac under Things worth knowing.
